newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai markets forge ahead as finance worries recede.
newsitem.headline: Thai markets forge ahead as finance worries recede.

text.p: Thai stock prices forged ahead for the third session in a row and the baht moved higher on Tuesday as worries over the health of the nation's financial system receded.

Traders said they were encouraged by news that the cabinet had approved plans for a bond issue of up to 100 billion baht ($3.87 billion) to bolster the crisis-torn property market, into which finance firms have poured a quarter of their loans.
Proceeds from the seven-year, zero-coupon bonds will be used to refinance troubled property projects and relieve a cash squeeze on their creditors.

"The authorities are confident that this measure will positively strengthen the financial condition of the property sector while further strengthening the soundness of Thailand's financial institutions," the central bank said in a statement.
The SET stock market index, supported by speculative buying ahead of the cabinet decision on the zero-coupon bond plan, gained nearly 1.4 percent in early trade.
By the midday break, it was up 7.85, or 1.12 percent, at 1,711.17.

But while the panic which triggered huge withdrawals from finance companies last week appeared to have subsided, investors still had nagging doubts over a possible downgrade of Thailand's debt ratings, slowing economic growth and faltering exports.
"The general consensus is that the government's measures are good," said Surakiat Wongwasin, president of Multi-Credit Corporation of Thailand.

"Personally, I think this is a technical rebound. The main figures to watch for now are January's economic figures," he said, referring to trade and current account data. "If they are not positive you could get another hiccup."
He said foreign speculators were still waiting in the wings to test the Bank of Thailand's resolve to defend the baht against devaluation.
Analysts said the central bank probably spent billions of dollars to fend of speculators between December and February.

The baht rose to 29.935-25.940 to the dollar from 25.937-25.942 late on Monday following a comment from Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond that the currency would be made more flexible to counter speculative attacks.
Rerngchai gave no details of how and when the baht, which is pegged daily against a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar, would be given a freer rein.
Analysts believe the central bank may widen the dollar/baht trading band, fix its official pivot rate more than once a day or reduce the dollar's weighting in the basket.

The cabinet also approved a proposal on Tuesday by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan to trim the 1996/97 (October/September) budget by 106 billion baht as part of a policy to rein in the current account deficit.

Merrill Lynch said in a report released on Monday that Thailand's economic fundamentals, although still fragile, were moving in the right direction and that financial firms would be able to weather any future storms.
"We think the probability of a vicious trap involving a banking crisis and a GDP slump...is low as Thai banks have priced loan risks appropriately in the past," it said.
